open_points.subject: State 6 source of truth
open_points.text: “The exact signatures are `60_contracts.json` ... [and the exact models and taxonomy are other named JSON files]. This text records the technical decisions those files rest on”
open_points.question: What are the exact signatures, argument and answer models, store payloads, and exception mappings when the named artifacts are not part of the accepted text available to later agents?
options: Include the referenced JSON artifacts as normative inputs
Reproduce their complete contracts in this text
Treat the State 5 prose as the contract and let each agent reconstruct the missing types
open_points.default_guess: Reconstruct the contracts from State 5 and the State 6 prose, despite the resulting implementation differences.

open_points.subject: State 6 status and revision
open_points.text: “Draft of 2026-10-03” while the same document contains decisions and amendments dated 2026-10-10
open_points.question: Is this complete 2026-10-10 document accepted and authoritative, or is it still a 2026-10-03 draft awaiting another acceptance step?
options: Accepted as amended through 2026-10-10
Draft as amended through 2026-10-10
Only the 2026-10-03 portion is authoritative
open_points.default_guess: Treat the entire document as authoritative through 2026-10-10.

open_points.subject: Supported JSON Schema subset
open_points.text: “a schema is a JSON object using only `type` ... `enum` ... `const` ... `properties` ...”
open_points.question: What exact schema dialect and structural rules apply: whether `type` is required, the permitted types and ranges of each keyword, compatible keyword combinations, the default for omitted `additionalProperties`, and the behavior of keywords used without their corresponding type?
options: Use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 semantics restricted to the listed keywords
Require `type` except for the file schema `{}` and define custom compatibility rules
Define a complete kernel-specific grammar and validation semantics
open_points.default_guess: Use Draft 2020-12 semantics restricted to the listed keywords, with omitted `type` unconstrained and omitted `additionalProperties` equal to true.

open_points.subject: Closed schemas used by guards
open_points.text: “A closed set (A05 guards) is a schema with `enum` or `const`.”
open_points.question: When a schema contains both `enum` and `const`, or combines either with other constraints, which values are members of the guard's closed set?
options: Use the intersection of every schema constraint
Use `const` when present and otherwise `enum`
Reject schemas that combine `const` and `enum` or constrain their members further
open_points.default_guess: Use the values satisfying the entire schema, i.e. the intersection of all constraints.

open_points.subject: File digests
open_points.text: “A `value` port's value travels as its RFC 8785 canonical bytes, a file as its bytes” does not state how `StoredValue.value_digest`, `SpooledFile.content_digest`, file facts, or file-output comparisons digest those bytes.
open_points.question: What exact byte sequence is hashed for a file fixture or spooled file?
options: SHA-256 of the raw file bytes
SHA-256 of canonical JSON containing base64 text
A carriage-specific structured digest including media type
open_points.default_guess: Use lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the raw file bytes; media type remains a separate fact.

open_points.subject: Surface authorization exceptions
open_points.text: “Refusals are exceptions ... one symbol per meaning” names `UnknownReferenceError`, `RefusedError`, `InvalidRequestError` and `StoreInternalError`, but State 5 also requires the distinct surface codes `unauthorized` and `not_permitted`.
open_points.question: Which exception or returned contract represents the `unauthorized` and `not_permitted` refusals so `surface.translate_failure` can distinguish them?
options: Add surface-owned `UnauthorizedError` and `NotPermittedError`
Return a typed `RefusalAnswer` directly from surface checks
Reuse named exceptions and add contextual mapping rules

open_points.subject: MCP listener start failure
open_points.text: State 5 requires an `mcp_listen_address` that cannot be parsed or bound to stop start with a named reason, while “Start-only refusals belong to their module” names only `InstallationRejectedError` and `SandboxUnavailableError`.
open_points.question: What contract or exception owns failure to parse or bind the MCP listener address?
options: A surface-owned start rejection exception
`RefusedError` raised by surface
A typed non-zero result returned by `serve_kernel`
open_points.default_guess: Use a surface-owned start rejection exception translated only at the host boundary.

open_points.subject: MCP release constants
open_points.text: “a POST to the path `MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH`” and “answers `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` ... `MCP_SERVER_NAME` / `MCP_SERVER_VERSION`” name constants without giving their release-v1 values or a configuration source.
open_points.question: What are the exact endpoint path, protocol version, server name and server version?
options: Fix literal release-v1 values in `data_provider`
Derive the server version from package metadata and fix the other literals
Add them to installation configuration
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed `data_provider` literals, with `/mcp` as the endpoint and the package release as the server version.

open_points.subject: JSON-RPC notifications that fail
open_points.text: “[a POST] is answered `202` without a body when the message is a notification” contradicts “A refusal decided before — size, token, a malformed message, unknown method or tool — is a JSON-RPC error”.
open_points.question: When a notification is malformed, unauthorized, names an unknown method or tool, or its operation refuses, does the server return an empty 202 or a JSON-RPC error response?
options: Every notification receives 202 with no body, including failures
Pre-dispatch failures return JSON-RPC errors but operation refusals return 202
Every failed notification returns a JSON-RPC error
open_points.default_guess: Follow JSON-RPC notification semantics: process it when possible but always return 202 without a JSON-RPC body.

open_points.subject: MCP HTTP request framing
open_points.text: “a POST ... carries one JSON-RPC 2.0 message” does not say which request `Content-Type` values or HTTP body framings are accepted.
open_points.question: Must a POST use `application/json` and `Content-Length`, and are chunked transfer encoding, content-type parameters, persistent connections, or bodies on other methods accepted?
options: Require `application/json` with optional charset and a valid bounded `Content-Length`; reject transfer encoding
Support both content length and chunked bodies
Ignore content type and accept any framing `http.server` can read
open_points.default_guess: Require a bounded `Content-Length`, accept `application/json` with no meaningful parameters, and reject chunked transfer encoding.

open_points.subject: Ownership of release pins
open_points.text: Decision 25 says the release pins are “`data_provider` constants”, while State 3 says “No module owns them ... `data_provider` holds no pin.”
open_points.question: Are sandbox, bwrap and Python-dependency pins runtime constants owned by `data_provider`, or release metadata outside every runtime module?
options: Amend State 3 so `data_provider` owns and exports the pins
Keep pins outside runtime and pass probe expectations into the modules
Split build metadata from only the runtime constants needed by the probe
open_points.default_guess: Amend State 3 so `data_provider` owns the constants required by `sandbox.probe_sandbox`, while build-only metadata stays outside runtime.
open_points.unit: 60_contracts.md:Decisions closed before the first Route B (2026-10-10)

open_points.subject: Sandbox runtime contents
open_points.text: Decision 25 makes `SANDBOX_RUNTIME_PATHS` equal to `("/usr")`, while A03 requires “one Python interpreter with its standard library and nothing else” and says no host directory is mounted except that read-only runtime.
open_points.question: How does mounting all of `/usr` prevent agent code from importing third-party packages or reaching other programs and files installed there?
options: Mount a release-built runtime containing only CPython and its standard library
Mount `/usr` but explicitly remove or mask every non-runtime path
Allow the extra read-only contents and amend A03's standard-library-only rule
open_points.default_guess: Use a release-built, read-only runtime tree containing only the pinned interpreter and standard library instead of the host's whole `/usr`.
open_points.unit: 60_contracts.md:Decisions closed before the first Route B (2026-10-10)

open_points.subject: MCP HTTP handler applicability
open_points.text: “No router handler is planned” conflicts with decision 22, which requires handling an MCP HTTP endpoint with POST, 202, 403, 404 and 405 behavior.
open_points.question: Is an HTTP request handler for the MCP transport part of `surface`, despite there being no separate application HTTP API?
options: Yes; model a surface-owned MCP transport handler while keeping all application operations internal-only
No; change the MCP transport away from streamable HTTP
Treat the handler as private implementation and remove the claim that no handler is planned
open_points.default_guess: Implement a private surface-owned MCP HTTP handler and interpret the exclusion as applying only to an application REST/router layer.
